cases.summary: The driver came within 24 m of the pickup point (well inside the 150 m threshold) and made a recorded contact attempt, but the GPS record shows only 210 seconds elapsed between first coming within 150 m and cancelling, short of the 300-second minimum required by NS-1. Because one of the three NS-1 conditions is not met, the no-show fee is not retainable under the demonstration policy and the paid S$5.00 fee is refundable under NS-2. The driver's position is therefore not defensible on the current evidence, and the appropriate outcome is a refund of the no-show fee.

arguments.claim: The driver satisfied the proximity condition: closest approach to the pickup was 24 m, within the 150 m NS-1 limit.
The driver satisfied the contact condition: one recorded contact attempt (CHAT-01, 'I'm here at the main entrance.') before cancelling, meeting the NS-1 minimum of one.
The driver marked arrived at 10:22:44Z and cancelled at 10:26:14Z, a wait of 210 seconds, which is less than the 300-second minimum required by NS-1.
Because not all three NS-1 conditions are met, the no-show fee cannot be retained and the exact paid fee of S$5.00 must be refunded under NS-2.

counterevidence.claim: The rider's own message at 10:25:14Z said 'Coming down now, 2 minutes!', indicating the rider was en route and would have arrived around 10:27:14Z, roughly one minute after the driver cancelled at 10:26:14Z; this supports the rider's account that the cancellation was premature.
The wait was only 210 seconds against a 300-second minimum, so the driver cancelled 90 seconds early; this is the decisive fact against retaining the fee.

missingFacts: Whether the driver attempted a phone call to the rider (callCount is 0), which could have extended the effective contact record.
Whether the pickup pin location was accurate relative to the rider's actual exit point, which could explain the rider's delay.
Whether any app notification or arrival alert was delivered to the rider at 10:22:44Z, which would bear on the rider's responsiveness.
The rider's exact arrival time at the pickup point, to assess whether the 300-second wait would have been satisfied had the driver waited longer.

cases.summary: The rider was charged a S$5.00 no-show fee, but the driver cancelled before the NS-1 minimum wait elapsed. GPS shows the driver came within 150 m (24 m closest approach) at 10:22:44Z and cancelled at 10:26:14Z, only 210 seconds later — short of the 300-second minimum. The rider also messaged at 10:25:14Z that they were coming down in 2 minutes, consistent with being en route. Because not all three NS-1 conditions are met, NS-2 requires a full refund of the paid no-show fee.

arguments.claim: The driver did not wait the required 300 seconds: GPS shows only 210 seconds between first coming within 150 m (10:22:44Z) and cancellation (10:26:14Z), so the NS-1 wait condition is NOT MET.

The rider was actively on their way down and communicated this: rider chat at 10:25:14Z said 'Coming down now, 2 minutes!', which is consistent with the rider's claim of being en route when the driver cancelled.
The rider was charged and paid a S$5.00 no-show fee, which is the exact amount eligible for refund under NS-2 because an NS-1 condition failed.

counterevidence.claim: The driver did satisfy the distance condition (24 m, within the 150 m limit) and made one recorded contact attempt ('I'm here at the main entrance.' at 10:23:14Z), meeting two of the three NS-1 conditions.
The driver's statement that they waited and the rider did not show is partially corroborated by the driver's arrival and contact attempt, though the wait duration falls short of policy.

missingFacts: Rider's exact location and movement toward the pickup between 10:22:44Z and cancellation, to confirm they were genuinely en route.
Whether the driver's marked arrival point (24 m from the pin) matched the rider's intended pickup spot, e.g. a specific entrance or door.
Any call attempts or additional messages not captured in the 2-message chat log.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. Retain the no-show fee only when the evidence shows all three conditions: the driver came within 150 metres of the pickup point; the driver waited at least 300 seconds from first coming within 150 metres until cancelling; and the driver made at least one recorded contact attempt (message or call) before cancelling.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when all three NS-1 conditions are met.

findings.claim: The driver did not satisfy the NS-1 waiting condition: GPS shows only 210 seconds between first coming within 150 m (10:22:44Z) and cancellation (10:26:14Z), short of the 300-second minimum.
The driver did satisfy the NS-1 distance condition (closest approach 24 m, within the 150 m limit).
The driver did satisfy the NS-1 contact condition: one recorded contact attempt before cancelling (CHAT-01), meeting the minimum of one.
Because one NS-1 condition (minimum wait) is not met, the no-show fee is not retainable and the exact paid S$5.00 fee is refundable under NS-2.
The rider messaged at 10:25:14Z that they were coming down in 2 minutes, consistent with being en route when the driver cancelled.

result.reasoning: NS-1 requires all three conditions for the no-show fee to be retained: within 150 m, waited at least 300 seconds, and at least one recorded contact attempt. GPS-PICKUP shows the distance condition MET (24 m) and CHAT-SUMMARY shows the contact condition MET (1 attempt, CHAT-01). However, GPS-PICKUP shows the wait condition NOT MET: only 210 seconds elapsed between first coming within 150 m (10:22:44Z) and cancellation (10:26:14Z), 90 seconds short of the 300-second minimum. Because any failed NS-1 condition triggers NS-2, the exact paid no-show fee of S$5.00 must be refunded. Payment evidence (PAY-FARE, PAY-REMEDY) confirms S$5.00 was paid and is the eligible refund amount. History and risk signals are context only and were not used to establish fault.

GPS shows the driver came within 24 m of the pickup at 10:22:44Z and cancelled at 10:26:14Z — only 210 seconds later, short of the 300-second minimum. Your message at 10:25:14Z saying you were coming down in 2 minutes supports that you were on your way. Because the waiting condition was not met, the no-show fee will be refunded in full.
result.driverExplanation: The no-show fee cannot be retained in this case. While you met two of the three required conditions — you came within 24 m of the pickup (within the 150 m limit) and made one recorded contact attempt — GPS shows you waited only 210 seconds from first coming within 150 m until cancelling, which is less than the 300-second minimum. Under the policy, failing any one of the three conditions means the paid no-show fee must be refunded to the rider.
